# Temple Scroll Column 66 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 66 | **Condition:** fragmentary toward end

---

**66:1** The LORD told me: What they said was right. I will raise up a prophet for them from among their own people, someone like you,

**66:2** and I will put my own words in his mouth. He will tell them everything I command him to say.

**66:3** If anyone refuses to listen to the words the prophet speaks in my name, I will personally hold that person to account.

**66:4** But if a prophet dares to speak in my name something I never told him to say, or speaks on behalf of other gods — that prophet must die.

**66:5** You may wonder: How do we tell whether a message really comes from the LORD?

**66:6** Here is the test: if a prophet speaks in the LORD's name and what he says does not happen or come true, the LORD did not send that message. That prophet spoke on his own authority. Do not be intimidated by him.

**66:7** When you have entered the land I am giving you and have settled there, and you decide you want a king like all the surrounding nations,

**66:8** you must appoint only the king I choose. He must be one of your own people — you must never put a foreigner over you who is not one of your brothers.

**66:9** The king must not build up a large stable of horses or send people back to Egypt to get more horses, because I have told you: You are never to go back that way.

**66:10** He must not take many wives, or his heart will be led astray. He must not accumulate vast amounts of silver and gold.

**66:11** When he takes the throne, he must write out his own copy of this law on a scroll, copying from the one kept by the Levitical priests.

**66:12** He must keep it with him and read from it every day of his life, so he will learn to respect the LORD his God by obeying every word of this law and these decrees,

**66:13** so he will not consider himself better than his fellow Israelites or turn from these commands in any way, [...] and so that he and his descendants will reign for a long time over Israel.

**66:14** [...] If you fully obey the LORD your God and carefully follow all his commands I am giving you today,

**66:15** [...] the LORD your God will raise you high above every other nation on earth.

**66:16** All these blessings will chase you down and overtake you, if you obey the LORD your God. [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 66 covers three major topics: how to spot a false prophet, what kind of king God wants, and the blessings for obedience. The king passage is remarkable — God personally selects the king, who must then hand-copy the law and read it daily. This is anti-monarchical in the best sense: the king is under the law, not above it. The blessings "chasing you down" (66:16) is a vivid Hebrew image worth preserving. Lacunae increase toward the column's end.*
